newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent unquoted but uptrend still expected.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent unquoted but uptrend still expected.

text.p: Brent crude oil futures in Asia were unquoted at midday on Tuesday, but brokers still see a bullish uptrend in prices which remain driven mainly by technicals.
London closed on Monday six cents lower at $18.93 per barrel.
But Brent's lowest level was $18.71, which brokers said is still above the $18.68 support level, and seen as a sign of a relatively strong market.
Brokers were also watching the outcome of the American Petroleum Institute (API) data, due out late Tuesday in the U.S.
A rise in crude stocks was likely, since European crudes, including Brent have been moving into the U.S.
But the impact of an increase in crude stocks is expected to be over shadowed by high refinery utilisation rates in the U.S, brokers said.
"Even if there was a two million build on crude stocks, prices should remain supported if refinery utilisation rates are still at 95-percent and above" said a broker in Singapore.
NYMEX crudes on ACCESS last traded at $19.99, up eight cents after New York fell 16 cents to settle at $19.91.
